sessions.title: The Founder's Guide to Shutting Down
sessions.description: Most startup content is about building. This one is about ending — cleanly and deliberately. Shutting down a company means navigating legal, tax, and compliance requirements at exactly the moment you have the least energy for them. Dori Yona built SimpleClosure to fix that. This roundtable is for founders who want to understand what a clean exit actually looks like — and how to close one chapter fast enough to open the next.

sessions.title: What Happens When You Replace Mortgage Infra
sessions.description: Figure originated $22 billion in home loans on blockchain rails. Valon built ValonOS and became a top 10 mortgage servicer with $110 billion under management. When they worked together, Valon-serviced loans showed a 40% improvement in delinquency outcomes and a 23.3x increase in originations. Mortgage is the largest consumer finance product in the US, running on software older than most people in this room. Michael Tannenbaum, Linda Du, and Rex Salisbury are here to explain how it gets fixed.

speakers.name: Dori Yona
speakers.title: CEO
speakers.bio: Dori Yona started SimpleClosure after facing a tough moment in his own business when he needed help closing down a company but couldn't find good advice anywhere. After running a company called Earny that millions of people used, he knew there had to be a better way to help business owners close their companies. Now, SimpleClosure helps founders shut down their companies faster and cheaper than traditional methods. Based in Santa Monica with his family, Dori works to show that closing a business doesn't have to be scary or hard, and that learning from tough experiences can lead to helping others.

speakers.bio: Danielle Madison is Co-Founder and Head of Partnerships at Forward, an Austin-based embedded payments company. After nearly two decades building software with deep ties to payments, Danielle and Forward's founding team had a successful exit to Fiserv. They went inside the payments giant and ran the integrated payments division, where it all clicked: no wonder it was so hard to get payments right all those years. Unfair economics, rigid technology, and a model that wasn't built for software companies. That experience became the catalyst for Forward, as in pay it Forward. Now as co-founder, Danielle partners with vertical SaaS platforms to help them unlock payments revenue through modern infrastructure and a true partnership model.
